blockers.title: The P-002-4 supersession still omits D-058's V1 coordinator owner.
evidence: P-002-4 says Operational metadata is 'not a grant journal', and D-058 owner-records that disposition under the exact role 'Evidence authority + V1 coordinator'.

The candidate now places P-002-4 in proposedSupersession.of, but its required concurrence list contains Semantic, Evidence, storage, operability, lifecycle, and DR-105 security/platform—not V1 coordinator.
The proposed D-096 (A) condition only promises coverage of every named role. Because V1 coordinator is not named, that condition cannot cure the omission.
blockers.impact: The stated apply path could overturn an owner-recorded P-002-4 bound without one of the two roles that recorded it. The supersession therefore remains unauthorized even if every listed role later concurs.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add V1 coordinator explicitly to ownersWhoseConcurrenceIsRequired and to any future user-express grant/recording preconditions. Preserve the existing statement that the candidate, reviews, and coordinator recording do not themselves supply concurrence or mint D-096 (A).

blockers.title: The local purge journal has no unambiguous sole writer and therefore no coherent FC-RO boundary.
evidence: Live DR-G19 requires every durable/rebuildable byte to have one declared class, owner, writer, and lifecycle; the candidate's own purpose repeats that closure goal.
The repaired row's soleWriterForTheseBytes is 'Core lifecycle / doctor owner for preview local journal bytes'. A slash between two actor surfaces does not select one writer.

Doctor v4 FC-RO binds doctor's own writes and requires every differing SC-OPS entry written by doctor to be accounted for by doctor's own invocation audit. The candidate instead enumerates the local purge journal among byte sets outside that conjunct. That is coherent only if doctor is not its writer, which the row does not say.
blockers.impact: A harness cannot tell whether a purge-journal write is a permitted core-lifecycle write outside FC-RO or a forbidden unaccounted doctor write. The repair assigns a class but still fails DR-124/DR-G19's one-writer closure.
blockers.requiredRepair: Name exactly one writer. If it is the core-lifecycle purge executor under the project/operation lock, state that doctor is not the writer and may write only its separate own-invocation audit. If doctor writes the purge journal, reconcile that write with FC-RO through the doctor-owned reviewed path. Keep authoritative purge result/exit semantics on DR-113 and mint no purge/D9 code.

blockers.title: The grant-journal carve-out contradicts SC-OPS boundedness outside the named supersession's scope.
evidence: The carried file-04 SC-OPS rule is 'Journaled/redacted/bounded'; owner-recorded P-002-4 and P-005-2 repeat that bound.
The DR-105 grant-journal classRuleCarveOut says sequence records MUST NOT be dropped or bounded away and that the journal is durable append-only.

proposedSupersession.whatIsSuperseded says 'Only the prohibition on SC-OPS containing the DR-105 grant journal' changes. It does not supersede boundedness, and the candidate supplies no bounded quota/refusal, checkpoint, archival, retention, or purge rule that preserves the required ordering records.
blockers.impact: The same byte set is simultaneously required to be bounded and forbidden from being bounded, while the purportedly closed supersession denies changing that rule. Retention, backup, and purge behavior are not derivable, so the SC-OPS placement is internally inconsistent.
blockers.requiredRepair: Either specify a bounded lifecycle that preserves the required durable order (including fail-closed behavior at any hard bound), or expand the named proposed supersession to cover the exact boundedness exception, its owner concurrence, scope, lifecycle consequences, and reversibility. Do not silently weaken the grant journal's ordering semantics.
